words.enDefinition: your closest relatives, such as parents, siblings, spouse and children

examples.en: Only immediate family members were invited to the small graduation dinner.
examples.zh: 那场小型毕业晚宴只邀请了「直系亲属」。

examples.en: On the emergency form, I listed my parents as my immediate family.
examples.zh: 紧急联系表上，我把父母填成了我的「直系亲属」。

words.enDefinition: relatives beyond your immediate family, like aunts, uncles and cousins

examples.en: My extended family flies in every Christmas, so the house gets crowded.
examples.zh: 每年圣诞节，我的「大家庭」亲戚都会飞过来，家里变得特别挤。

examples.en: Growing up with an extended family nearby taught me to share everything.
examples.zh: 从小身边就有「大家庭」的亲戚，让我学会了分享一切。

words.enDefinition: a family unit of parents and their children only

examples.en: In the city, most students I know come from a nuclear family.
examples.zh: 在城市里，我认识的大多数同学都来自「核心家庭」。

examples.en: A nuclear family usually finds it easier to move for work.
examples.zh: 「核心家庭」通常更容易为了工作而搬家。

collocations: grow up in a nuclear family

words.enDefinition: a chart showing how your family members are related

examples.en: For our writing class, I had to draw my family tree back three generations.
examples.zh: 写作课作业要求我把「家谱」画到上三代。

examples.en: Talking with my grandmother filled in the missing branches of our family tree.
examples.zh: 和奶奶聊天，补全了我们「家谱」上缺失的分支。

words.enDefinition: an event where relatives spend time together

examples.en: Every Mid-Autumn Festival, our family gathering fills my parents' apartment with noise.
examples.zh: 每年中秋，我们的「家庭聚会」都会让我父母的公寓热闹非凡。

examples.en: I skipped a club party because my family gathering ran late.
examples.zh: 我没去社团派对，因为「家庭聚会」拖得太晚。

words.enDefinition: an occasion when scattered relatives come together again

examples.en: Our family reunion at my aunt's farmhouse lasted the whole weekend.
examples.zh: 在姑妈农庄举办的「家庭团聚」持续了整个周末。

examples.en: Graduation week doubles as a family reunion for many international students.
examples.zh: 对很多留学生来说，毕业周同时也是一次「家庭团聚」。

words.enDefinition: a similar appearance shared by people in one family

examples.en: The family resemblance between you and your sister is impossible to miss.
examples.zh: 你和姐姐「一家人长得像」这一点，想忽视都难。

examples.en: People point out the family resemblance whenever my cousins visit campus.
examples.zh: 每次表哥们来学校，大家都会说我们「一家人长得像」。

words.enDefinition: the relatives of your husband or wife

examples.en: My in-laws are visiting this weekend, so the apartment must be spotless.
examples.zh: 这周末我的「姻亲」要来，家里必须一尘不染。

examples.en: Getting along with your in-laws takes patience and honest communication.
examples.zh: 和「姻亲」相处好需要耐心和坦诚的沟通。

words.enDefinition: the mother of your husband or wife

examples.en: My mother-in-law taught me her dumpling recipe over a video call.
examples.zh: 「岳母」在视频通话里教了我她包饺子的配方。

examples.en: Getting along with my mother-in-law got easier once we cooked together.
examples.zh: 一起下厨之后，我和「婆婆」相处轻松多了。

words.enDefinition: the father of your husband or wife

examples.en: My father-in-law picked us up from the airport with a homemade sign.
examples.zh: 我的「岳父」举着一块手写的牌子来机场接我们。

examples.en: My father-in-law helped us move into the new apartment last month.
examples.zh: 上个月，我的「公公」帮我们搬进了新公寓。

words.enDefinition: the brother of your spouse, or your sibling's husband

examples.en: My brother-in-law drove four hours to help me move into my dorm.
examples.zh: 我的「姐夫」开了四个小时的车，帮我把行李搬进宿舍。

examples.en: During the holidays, my brother-in-law always organizes the basketball game.
examples.zh: 放假时，我的「小叔」总是组织大家一起打篮球。

words.enDefinition: the sister of your spouse, or your sibling's wife

examples.en: My sister-in-law sent me a care package before finals week.
examples.zh: 期末周前，我的「嫂子」给我寄了一个关怀包裹。

examples.en: I practiced my English with my sister-in-law during the wedding weekend.
examples.zh: 婚礼那个周末，我和「小姑」一起练习英语。

words.enDefinition: your father's new wife after a divorce or remarriage

examples.en: My stepmother picked me up from the airport when my dad was busy.
examples.zh: 爸爸没空的时候，是「继母」来机场接的我。

examples.en: It took a year, but my stepmother and I finally get along well.
examples.zh: 虽然花了一年时间，但我和「继母」终于相处得很好。

words.enDefinition: your mother's new husband after a divorce or remarriage

examples.en: My stepfather taught me how to drive in the empty parking lot.
examples.zh: 「继父」在空旷的停车场教我开车。

examples.en: I call my stepfather by his first name, and he doesn't mind.
examples.zh: 我直呼「继父」的名字，他也并不介意。

words.enDefinition: the son of your step-parent, not related by blood

examples.en: My stepbrother is a sophomore here, so we grab lunch sometimes.
examples.zh: 我的「继兄弟」就在这所学校读大二，所以我们有时会一起吃午饭。

examples.en: I share a room with my stepbrother when I visit my dad.
examples.zh: 回爸爸家的时候，我和「继弟」睡同一个房间。

collocations: share a room with my stepbrother

words.enDefinition: the daughter of your step-parent, not related by blood

examples.en: My stepsister helped me choose courses before the semester started.
examples.zh: 开学前，「继姐」帮我选好了课。

examples.en: My stepsister and I text almost every day even though we live apart.
examples.zh: 虽然住得远，我和「继妹」几乎每天都发消息。

words.enDefinition: the son of your husband or wife from an earlier marriage

examples.en: My uncle's stepson joined us for Thanksgiving dinner this year.
examples.zh: 今年感恩节，我叔叔的「继子」和我们一起吃了晚饭。

examples.en: Our host family introduced us to their teenage stepson at dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭时，寄宿家庭向我们介绍了他们十几岁的「继子」。

words.enDefinition: the daughter of your husband or wife from an earlier marriage

examples.en: Her stepdaughter studies art, so they visit the museum together.
examples.zh: 她的「继女」学艺术，所以她们常常一起逛博物馆。

examples.en: The professor mentioned his stepdaughter during the campus family day.
examples.zh: 校园家庭日上，教授提到了他的「继女」。

words.zhGloss: 同父异母或同母异父的兄弟
words.enDefinition: a brother who shares only one parent with you
acceptedZhAnswers: 同父异母或同母异父的兄弟

examples.en: My half-brother lives with our dad in Vancouver, so we video chat weekly.
examples.zh: 我「同父异母的弟弟」和爸爸住在温哥华，我们每周都会视频。

examples.en: People think we're just cousins until I explain he's my half-brother.
examples.zh: 大家以为我们只是表兄弟，直到我解释他是我「同母异父的哥哥」。

words.zhGloss: 同父异母或同母异父的姐妹
words.enDefinition: a sister who shares only one parent with you
acceptedZhAnswers: 同父异母或同母异父的姐妹

examples.en: My baby half-sister was born the year I left for university.
examples.zh: 我去上大学那年，我「同父异母的妹妹」出生了。

examples.en: During spring break, I babysat my little half-sister for two days.
examples.zh: 春假期间，我照顾了「同母异父的小妹妹」两天。

collocations: half-sister from my dad's second marriage

words.enDefinition: a family formed when parents with children remarry each other

examples.en: As a blended family, we celebrate two sets of holiday traditions.
examples.zh: 身为「重组家庭」，我们保留着两边的节日传统。

examples.en: Adjusting to a blended family takes time, especially for teenagers.
examples.zh: 适应「重组家庭」需要时间，对青少年来说尤其如此。

collocations: a blended family with two kids

words.enDefinition: one of two twins from the same egg who look the same

examples.en: My roommates are identical twins, and even the professor mixes them up.
examples.zh: 我的室友们是「同卵双胞胎」，连教授都会认错。

examples.en: Telling my identical twin classmates apart took me a whole month.
examples.zh: 分辨我那对「同卵双胞胎」同学，花了我整整一个月。

words.enDefinition: one of two twins who develop from two different eggs

examples.en: My fraternal twin sister and I took completely different majors.
examples.zh: 我和「异卵双胞胎」姐姐选了完全不同的专业。

examples.en: Unlike identical twins, fraternal twins can look completely different from each other.
examples.zh: 和同卵双胞胎不同，「异卵双胞胎」可能长得完全不一样。

words.enDefinition: a brother or sister who shares your parents

examples.en: Being an only child, I always wished I had a sibling to play with.
examples.zh: 作为独生子女，我一直希望有个「兄弟姐妹」陪自己玩。

examples.en: Sibling rivalry got intense whenever my brother borrowed my laptop.
examples.zh: 弟弟一借走我的电脑，我们「手足之间」就免不了一番较量。

words.enDefinition: a child with no brothers or sisters

examples.en: As an only child, I learned to entertain myself with books.
examples.zh: 作为「独生子女」，我从小学会用书打发时间。

examples.en: My roommate grew up as an only child, so sharing felt strange at first.
examples.zh: 我的室友是「独生子女」，一开始不太习惯和人分享。

collocations: grow up as an only child
the only child of my parents

words.enDefinition: the first-born child among the children in a family

examples.en: As the oldest child, I helped my parents raise my younger brothers.
examples.zh: 作为「家里的老大」，我帮父母带大了弟弟们。

examples.en: The oldest child in my host family leaves for college next fall.
examples.zh: 我寄宿家庭的「老大」明年秋天就要去上大学了。

words.enDefinition: a child born between an older and a younger sibling

examples.en: As the middle child, my sister says nobody took her photos.
examples.zh: 身为「中间的孩子」，我姐姐说小时候家里没人给她拍照。

examples.en: Middle child syndrome jokes follow my brother at every dinner table.
examples.zh: 每次家庭聚餐，「老二综合征」的玩笑都会落到我弟弟头上。

words.enDefinition: a family member not closely related, like a second cousin

examples.en: A distant relative from Chengdu reached out before my campus visit.
examples.zh: 我来学校参观之前，一位成都的「远亲」联系了我。

examples.en: We invited every distant relative we could find to grandma's ninetieth birthday.
examples.zh: 奶奶九十大寿，我们把能找到的「远房亲戚」都请来了。

collocations: a distant relative on my mother's side

words.enDefinition: a person related to you by birth, not marriage

examples.en: Adoption made him family even without being a blood relative.
examples.zh: 领养让他成了家人，尽管并非「血亲」。

examples.en: The form asked whether my emergency contact was a blood relative.
examples.zh: 表格询问我的紧急联系人是不是「血亲」。

collocations: blood relatives on my father's side

words.enDefinition: your closest relative, listed for emergencies on official forms

examples.en: Universities ask international students to list next of kin on enrollment forms.
examples.zh: 学校要求留学生在注册表上填写「最近亲属」。

examples.en: The hospital called my next of kin after my appendix surgery.
examples.zh: 阑尾手术后，医院联系了我的「最近亲属」。

words.enDefinition: a family member who lived long before you

examples.en: My ancestors moved to this coastal town over two hundred years ago.
examples.zh: 两百多年前，我的「祖先」搬到了这座海滨小镇。

examples.en: During Qingming, our family honors ancestors with a simple home ritual.
examples.zh: 清明时节，我们全家会用简单的仪式祭拜「祖先」。

words.enDefinition: a person born in a later generation of a family

examples.en: As the youngest descendant, I inherited grandma's handwritten recipe book.
examples.zh: 作为最小的「后代」，我继承了奶奶的手写菜谱。

examples.en: The festival gathers descendants of the village's founding families every summer.
examples.zh: 每年夏天，节日都会聚集起村里创始家族的「后代」。

words.enDefinition: differences in views between older and younger generations

examples.en: The generation gap shows whenever my parents discuss my career plans.
examples.zh: 每当父母讨论我的职业规划，「代沟」就显现出来。

examples.en: Video calls helped narrow the generation gap between me and my grandfather.
examples.zh: 视频通话缩小了我和爷爷之间的「代沟」。

words.enDefinition: resemble an older family member in looks or character

examples.en: Everyone says I take after my mom, especially her stubborn streak.
examples.zh: 大家都说我「随我妈」，尤其是那股倔劲。

examples.en: Do you take after your father's side or your mother's side?
examples.zh: 你「随」爸爸这边还是妈妈这边？

words.enDefinition: a married woman's family surname before marriage

examples.en: The professor goes by her maiden name on all published papers.
examples.zh: 这位教授发表的所有论文都用她的「婚前姓氏」。

examples.en: I found grandma's maiden name in the old immigration records.
examples.zh: 我在旧的移民档案里查到了奶奶的「娘家姓」。

words.enDefinition: adults who temporarily care for children not their own

examples.en: My foster parents drove six hours so I could visit my birth grandmother.
examples.zh: 为了让我探望亲奶奶，我的「寄养父母」开车开了六个小时。

examples.en: Her foster parents encouraged her to apply for the scholarship abroad.
examples.zh: 她的「寄养父母」鼓励她申请出国奖学金。

words.enDefinition: legally take another person's child into your family

examples.en: My parents decided to adopt after volunteering at the orphanage.
examples.zh: 在孤儿院做志愿者之后，我父母决定「收养」孩子。

examples.en: They adopted a two-year-old girl from a city near my hometown.
examples.zh: 他们从我家乡附近的城市「领养」了一个两岁的女孩。

words.enDefinition: the parents someone was born to, by blood

examples.en: He finally met his biological parents at twenty-two through a DNA website.
examples.zh: 二十二岁那年，他通过 DNA 网站见到了自己的「亲生父母」。

examples.en: My adoptive parents always answered my questions about my biological parents honestly.
examples.zh: 关于「亲生父母」的问题，我的养父母总是坦诚作答。

words.enDefinition: the way someone was raised and cared for as a child

examples.en: My strict upbringing meant homework came before any screen time.
examples.zh: 我从小受到的「教养」很严格，写作业永远排在玩之前。

examples.en: A multicultural upbringing helped her adapt to campus life quickly.
examples.zh: 多元的「成长背景」让她很快适应了校园生活。

words.enDefinition: the promise to marry, often marked with a ring

examples.en: My sister announced her engagement during our video call last night.
examples.zh: 昨晚视频通话时，我姐姐宣布了「订婚」的消息。

examples.en: Grandma still wears the simple ring from her 1960s engagement.
examples.zh: 奶奶还戴着六十年代「订婚」时的素圈戒指。

words.enDefinition: the legal and social relationship between two married people

examples.en: Their marriage stayed strong through three years in different cities.
examples.zh: 异地三年，他们的「婚姻」依然稳固。

examples.en: In my culture, a marriage usually brings both big families together.
examples.zh: 在我的文化里，一场「婚姻」通常会让两个大家庭走到一起。

words.enDefinition: a person who shares your room or apartment

examples.en: My roommate and I split the groceries and cleaning duties evenly.
examples.zh: 我和「室友」平分买菜和打扫的任务。

examples.en: My roommate is a night owl, so I bought an eye mask.
examples.zh: 我的「室友」是个夜猫子，所以我买了个眼罩。

words.enDefinition: British word for someone sharing a rented flat

examples.en: My flatmate leaves sticky notes on the fridge to divide chores.
examples.zh: 我的「合租室友」会在冰箱上贴便利贴来分工。

examples.en: We found a flatmate through the university housing group chat.
examples.zh: 我们通过学校的租房群聊找到了一位「合租室友」。

words.enDefinition: someone you share a rented house with

examples.en: My housemate takes out the trash, and I handle the bathroom.
examples.zh: 我的「合住室友」负责倒垃圾，我负责打扫浴室。

examples.en: We interviewed three candidates before finally choosing our new housemate.
examples.zh: 我们面试了三个人，才最终选定新的「合住室友」。

words.enDefinition: a person living next door or very near you

examples.en: Our neighbor waters my plants whenever I fly home for the holidays.
examples.zh: 每次我回国过节，「邻居」都会帮我浇花。

examples.en: A noise complaint from our neighbor arrived the night before my exam.
examples.zh: 考试前一晚，「邻居」还投诉了我们太吵。

words.enDefinition: the person living in the house or room beside yours

examples.en: My next-door neighbor knocked to share homemade dumplings last Friday.
examples.zh: 上周五，「隔壁邻居」敲门送来了自己包的饺子。

examples.en: The next-door neighbor collects my packages whenever I'm in class.
examples.zh: 我上课的时候，「隔壁邻居」会帮我收快递。

collocations: ask the next-door neighbor for help

words.enDefinition: a person you know slightly, but not a close friend

examples.en: He's more of an acquaintance than a friend; we only nod in lectures.
examples.zh: 他算是「熟人」，算不上朋友——我们只在课堂上点个头。

examples.en: I ran into an acquaintance from my chemistry lab at the mall.
examples.zh: 我在商场碰到了一位实验课认识的「熟人」。

words.enDefinition: the friend you are closest to of all

examples.en: My best friend from high school videos with me every Sunday night.
examples.zh: 高中时的「挚友」每周日晚都和我视频。

examples.en: My roommate became my best friend within one stressful semester.
examples.zh: 一个紧张忙碌的学期下来，我的室友变成了我的「挚友」。

words.enDefinition: a friend you share personal thoughts and time with

examples.en: Only my close friends knew I was applying to programs abroad.
examples.zh: 只有几个「好友」知道我在申请出国的项目。

examples.en: She's a close friend, so I didn't mind picking her up at dawn.
examples.zh: 她是我的「好友」，所以天没亮去接她我也乐意。

words.enDefinition: a person who is a friend of both you and someone else

examples.en: A mutual friend introduced us during the first week of orientation.
examples.zh: 迎新周期间，一位「共同的朋友」介绍我们认识。

examples.en: We discovered a mutual friend while comparing our hometowns on the train.
examples.zh: 火车上聊起各自的家乡，我们发现彼此有位「共同的朋友」。

words.enDefinition: a friend you have known since you were a child

examples.en: My childhood friend still sends me photos of our old neighborhood.
examples.zh: 我的「发小」还会给我发老街区的照片。

examples.en: I stayed with a childhood friend during my first week in Boston.
examples.zh: 到波士顿的第一周，我借住在一位「发小」家里。

collocations: childhood friend from the same block

words.enDefinition: the group of people you regularly spend time with

examples.en: Joining the hiking club expanded my circle of friends beyond my major.
examples.zh: 加入远足社团，让我的「朋友圈子」不再局限于同专业同学。

examples.en: Our circle of friends meets every Friday for hotpot night.
examples.zh: 我们的「朋友圈子」每周五晚上聚在一起吃火锅。

words.enDefinition: an informal word for a friend or partner in an activity

examples.en: My gym buddy waits for me at six every morning.
examples.zh: 我的健身「伙伴」每天早上六点都在等我。

examples.en: I signed up as a study buddy for the freshmen orientation program.
examples.zh: 我报名当了迎新项目的「学习伙伴」。

words.enDefinition: a person you invite to visit your home

examples.en: We always give our guests the comfy sofa and the good snacks.
examples.zh: 我们总是把舒服的沙发和好吃的零食留给「客人」。

examples.en: My host family treats every guest like a member of the family.
examples.zh: 我的寄宿家庭把每一位「客人」都当家人对待。

words.enDefinition: a person you do not know at all

examples.en: My mom taught me never to share my address with strangers.
examples.zh: 妈妈从小教我，不要把住址告诉「陌生人」。

examples.en: A kind stranger helped me carry my suitcases up the station stairs.
examples.zh: 一位好心的「陌生人」帮我把行李箱抬上了车站的楼梯。

words.enDefinition: someone who has recently arrived in a place or group

examples.en: As a newcomer to the lab, I asked endless questions my first week.
examples.zh: 作为实验室的「新来的人」，第一周我问了无数个问题。

examples.en: The club pairs each newcomer with a senior student as a guide.
examples.zh: 社团会给每位「新成员」配一位学长学姐带路。

words.enDefinition: a person who feels drained by lots of social contact

examples.en: As an introvert, I need quiet time alone to recharge after club fairs.
examples.zh: 作为「内向的人」，社团招新之后我需要安静地独处充电。

examples.en: My introvert roommate makes friends slowly but keeps them forever.
examples.zh: 我的室友是个「内向的人」，交朋友慢，但一交就是长久的朋友。

words.enDefinition: a person who gains energy from being around people

examples.en: Being an extrovert, my brother chats with everyone in the elevator.
examples.zh: 我弟弟是个「外向的人」，连坐电梯都会跟人聊起来。

examples.en: Extroverts usually break the ice first at the orientation events.
examples.zh: 迎新活动上，「外向的人」通常第一个打破沉默。

words.enDefinition: someone who enjoys company and connects with others easily

examples.en: My aunt is a people person; strangers become her friends in minutes.
examples.zh: 我姑姑是个「善于交际的人」，陌生人几分钟就能聊成熟人。

examples.en: Being a people person helped her land the campus tour guide job.
examples.zh: 因为「善于交际」，她拿到了校园讲解员的兼职。

words.enDefinition: a person who prefers staying home to going out

examples.en: I'm a homebody, so I host movie nights instead of bar crawls.
examples.zh: 我是个「宅人」，所以宁愿办电影夜也不去泡吧。

examples.en: My homebody roommate cooks an elaborate dinner every single weekend.
examples.zh: 我那位「宅人」室友每个周末都会做一顿大餐。

words.enDefinition: a person who likes waking up and acting early

examples.en: As an early bird, I finish my essays before my roommates wake up.
examples.zh: 作为「早起的人」，我在室友们醒来前就写完了论文。

examples.en: The library is quiet at seven, perfect for early birds like me.
examples.zh: 早上七点的图书馆很安静，正适合我这样的「早鸟」。

words.enDefinition: a person others admire and want to imitate

examples.en: My older cousin was my role model for applying to universities abroad.
examples.zh: 我的表哥是我申请出国留学的「榜样」。

examples.en: Good role models matter more to teenagers than strict rules.
examples.zh: 对青少年来说，好的「榜样」比严格的规矩更重要。

collocations: be a role model to someone
look up to a role model

words.enDefinition: friendly and energetic, comfortable around new people

examples.en: My outgoing roommate organized a floor dinner during our first week.
examples.zh: 我那位「外向的」室友在开学第一周就组织了楼层聚餐。

examples.en: Outgoing people often become the glue of a student club.
examples.zh: 「外向的人」常常是一个社团的黏合剂。

words.enDefinition: nervous and quiet when meeting new people

examples.en: I was too shy to introduce myself on the first day of class.
examples.zh: 开学第一天，我「害羞」得不敢自我介绍。

examples.en: My shy deskmate opened up once we started studying together.
examples.zh: 一起自习之后，我那位「腼腆的」同桌慢慢放开了。

words.enDefinition: enjoying talking a lot with other people

examples.en: Our talkative taxi driver shared his whole life story on the ride.
examples.zh: 我们那位「健谈的」出租车司机一路讲完了自己的人生故事。

examples.en: The talkative guy in my dorm makes silence impossible at meetings.
examples.zh: 宿舍里那位「话多的」同学让会议根本安静不下来。

words.enDefinition: liking casual and friendly conversation

examples.en: The chatty barista remembers every regular customer's usual order by heart.
examples.zh: 那位「爱聊天的」咖啡师记得每位常客的固定口味。

examples.en: My chatty aunt turns every family dinner into a story session.
examples.zh: 我那位「爱聊天的」姑姑总能把家宴变成故事会。

words.enDefinition: clever and funny with words

examples.en: His witty replies keep our group chat lively at midnight.
examples.zh: 他「风趣的」回复让我们的群聊在午夜依然热闹。

examples.en: The witty host made every campus tour feel like a comedy show.
examples.zh: 那位「风趣的」讲解员让每次校园导览都像看脱口秀。

words.enDefinition: bad-tempered and easily irritated, especially in the morning

examples.en: Dad is grumpy until he finishes his first cup of coffee.
examples.zh: 爸爸喝完第一杯咖啡之前总是「脾气暴躁」。

examples.en: Our grumpy neighbor complains if we laugh too loudly on the balcony.
examples.zh: 只要我们在阳台笑得太大声，「暴躁的」邻居就会来抱怨。

words.enDefinition: changing moods quickly without an obvious reason

examples.en: My moody cousin can be hilarious one minute and silent the next.
examples.zh: 我那位「喜怒无常的」表哥前一分钟还笑得停不下来，下一分钟就沉默了。

examples.en: Teenagers can get moody sometimes, and that is completely normal.
examples.zh: 青少年有时会变得「情绪化」，这完全正常。

words.enDefinition: easily hurt by criticism or upset by small things

examples.en: She is sensitive about her accent, so avoid joking about it.
examples.zh: 她对自己的口音很「敏感」，别拿这个开玩笑。

examples.en: My sensitive little brother cried at the end of every cartoon.
examples.zh: 我「敏感的」弟弟看动画片结尾都会哭。

words.enDefinition: showing good judgment and practical thinking

examples.en: My sensible roommate suggested we write a cleaning schedule instead of arguing.
examples.zh: 我那「明事理的」室友提议列一张打扫值日表，而不是争吵。

examples.en: A sensible choice is texting your host family before you arrive late.
examples.zh: 「明智」的做法是，会晚到就提前告诉寄宿家庭。

words.enDefinition: getting angry quickly and easily

examples.en: Dad gets short-tempered whenever he drives in heavy city traffic.
examples.zh: 爸爸在市区堵车时特别「容易发火」。

examples.en: My short-tempered lab partner apologized right after snapping at us.
examples.zh: 我那位「容易发火的」实验搭档冲我们发完火，马上就道歉了。

words.enDefinition: relaxed and not easily worried or stressed

examples.en: My laid-back host dad never panics, even when flights get delayed.
examples.zh: 我那位「悠闲随和的」寄宿爸爸，就算航班延误也从不慌张。

examples.en: My housemates are so laid-back that exam weeks never feel scary.
examples.zh: 我的室友们都那么「悠闲随和」，考试周一点也不可怕。

words.enDefinition: friendly and easy to talk to

examples.en: Our advisor is approachable, so students drop by without appointments.
examples.zh: 我们的导师很「平易近人」，学生不预约也会来找他。

examples.en: The new librarian seems strict, but she's actually very approachable.
examples.zh: 新来的图书管理员看着严肃，其实非常「平易近人」。

words.enDefinition: kind and helpful about other people's needs

examples.en: My caring aunt drove two hours to deliver my forgotten passport.
examples.zh: 我那「有爱心的」姑姑开了两小时车，给我送来忘带的护照。

examples.en: Nursing attracts caring people who genuinely enjoy helping patients recover.
examples.zh: 护理行业吸引的是真心乐于帮病人康复的「有爱心的人」。

words.enDefinition: always ready to help and encourage others

examples.en: My parents were supportive when I chose an arts major.
examples.zh: 我选艺术专业时，父母非常「支持」我。

examples.en: A supportive roommate makes homesickness much easier to deal with.
examples.zh: 一位「给予支持的」室友能让想家的日子好过得多。

words.enDefinition: willing to forgive and consider others' feelings

examples.en: My understanding professor let me submit the essay one day late.
examples.zh: 我那位「善解人意的」教授允许我晚一天交论文。

examples.en: An understanding landlady reduced our rent during the tough month.
examples.zh: 那位「体谅人的」房东太太在我们最艰难的那个月减了房租。

words.enDefinition: honest and reliable, safe to trust with secrets

examples.en: I only lend my laptop to classmates I find truly trustworthy.
examples.zh: 我只把电脑借给我认为真正「值得信赖的」同学。

examples.en: A trustworthy friend keeps your secrets even after you argue.
examples.zh: 「值得信赖的朋友」就算和你吵过架也会守住秘密。

words.enDefinition: able to be trusted to do what you promise

examples.en: My dependable cousin picked me up at 5 a.m. without complaining.
examples.zh: 我那「靠得住的」表哥早上五点来接我，毫无怨言。

examples.en: Every team needs one dependable member who never misses deadlines.
examples.zh: 每个团队都需要一位从不误事、「靠得住」的成员。

words.enDefinition: working with energy and effort for long periods

examples.en: My hardworking mother ran the family shop while studying English at night.
examples.zh: 我「勤奋的」妈妈一边照看家里的店，一边晚上学英语。

examples.en: The hardworking student wiped tables to pay for her textbooks.
examples.zh: 那位「勤奋的」学生靠擦桌子挣出了课本钱。

words.enDefinition: strongly wanting to achieve success or goals

examples.en: My ambitious brother is already planning his startup before graduation.
examples.zh: 我那「有上进心的」弟弟还没毕业就开始筹划创业了。

examples.en: Ambitious students often pack their schedules with internships and certificates.
examples.zh: 「上进心强的」学生通常把日程排满了实习和考证。

words.enDefinition: working carefully and steadily without giving up

examples.en: Diligent evening revision finally pulled my grades up a level.
examples.zh: 每晚「勤奋刻苦的」复习，终于让我的成绩上了一个台阶。

examples.en: My diligent deskmate reviews vocabulary for twenty minutes after dinner daily.
examples.zh: 我那「勤勉的」同桌每天晚饭后复习二十分钟单词。

words.enDefinition: shy and lacking confidence to speak or act

examples.en: The timid freshman whispered her question after the lecture ended.
examples.zh: 那位「胆怯的」新生等讲座结束了才小声提出问题。

examples.en: Even now, my timid puppy hides whenever the doorbell rings.
examples.zh: 直到现在，我那只「胆小的」狗一听门铃就躲起来。

words.enDefinition: not bragging about your own achievements

examples.en: Despite winning the scholarship, she stayed humble about her grades.
examples.zh: 尽管拿了奖学金，她对成绩依然十分「谦虚」。

examples.en: My humble uncle credits his team whenever people praise his shop.
examples.zh: 每当有人夸店，我「谦虚的」叔叔总把功劳归于团队。

words.enDefinition: behaving as if you are better than everyone else

examples.en: The arrogant senior refused to explain anything to the freshmen.
examples.zh: 那位「自大的」学长什么都不肯教给新生。

examples.en: He sounded arrogant when he called everyone else's ideas basic.
examples.zh: 他说别人的想法都很普通时，听起来特别「傲慢」。

words.enDefinition: caring only about yourself and not others

examples.en: It felt selfish to keep the bigger room without asking my housemate.
examples.zh: 不问室友就占了那个大房间，我自觉很「自私」。

examples.en: Selfish roommates leave dishes for others to wash every night.
examples.zh: 「自私的」室友每晚都把碗留给别人洗。

words.enDefinition: behaving in a childish, less grown-up way

examples.en: Pranking the RA felt funny then, but it was pretty immature.
examples.zh: 捉弄宿管当时觉得好玩，但确实挺「不成熟」的。

examples.en: My immature cousin still hides his sister's shoes before school.
examples.zh: 我那「不成熟的」表弟上学前还会藏姐姐的鞋。

words.enDefinition: thinking and behaving like a responsible adult

examples.en: Living alone made me more mature about money and time.
examples.zh: 独自生活让我在花钱和时间安排上更「成熟」了。

examples.en: The mature way she handled the conflict impressed our advisor.
examples.zh: 她处理矛盾的「成熟」方式让导师印象深刻。

words.enDefinition: behaving like a young child, in a negative way

examples.en: Ignoring her texts for a week was a childish way to handle it.
examples.zh: 一周不回她消息，这种处理方式太「幼稚」了。

examples.en: Their childish argument over the TV remote lasted three days.
examples.zh: 他们为遥控器爆发的「孩子气」争吵持续了三天。

words.enDefinition: lacking experience, so believing things too easily

examples.en: I was naive to lend money without even a text message as proof.
examples.zh: 连个短信凭证都没有就把钱借出去，我实在太「天真」了。

examples.en: New students can seem naive about rental contracts and deposits.
examples.zh: 新生面对租房合同和押金，常常显得「涉世未深」。

words.enDefinition: noticing what others need and acting kindly

examples.en: It was thoughtful of my neighbor to water my plants during break.
examples.zh: 假期里邻居帮我浇花，真是「体贴周到」。

examples.en: A thoughtful housemate left cough drops on my desk when I was sick.
examples.zh: 我生病时，「体贴的」室友在我桌上留了润喉糖。

words.enDefinition: forgetful because your mind is on something else

examples.en: My absent-minded professor once taught the whole class with slippers on.
examples.zh: 我那位「心不在焉的」教授有一次穿着拖鞋上完了整节课。

examples.en: Absorbed in his novel, my absent-minded uncle missed his highway exit.
examples.zh: 我「心不在焉的」叔叔看小说入了迷，错过了高速出口。

words.enDefinition: willing to consider new ideas and different views

examples.en: My open-minded host family tried cooking dumplings for Spring Festival.
examples.zh: 我「思想开明的」寄宿家庭为了春节试着包了饺子。

examples.en: Studying abroad is easier if you stay open-minded about food customs.
examples.zh: 如果对饮食习俗保持「开放心态」，留学会轻松许多。

words.enDefinition: practical and realistic, without pretending to be special

examples.en: My down-to-earth advisor told me exactly which deadlines actually matter.
examples.zh: 我那位「接地气的」导师会直接告诉我哪些截止日期才真正要紧。

examples.en: Our coach has national medals, yet he is surprisingly down-to-earth.
examples.zh: 我们教练拿过全国奖牌，为人却出奇地「接地气」。

words.enDefinition: hard to please, especially about small details

examples.en: My picky roommate returns soup if the noodles are too soft.
examples.zh: 我那位「挑剔的」室友嫌面太软，会把汤退回去。

examples.en: Don't be picky about dorms in your first year; apply early instead.
examples.zh: 大一别对宿舍太「挑剔」，尽早申请才对。

words.enDefinition: nervous and unable to relax

examples.en: Don't get uptight about the presentation; even seniors stumble sometimes.
examples.zh: 别对这次演讲这么「紧绷」，学长们也常有失误。

examples.en: My roommate gets uptight whenever the floor meeting starts five minutes late.
examples.zh: 楼层会议晚开始五分钟，我的室友就「紧张拘谨」得不行。

words.enDefinition: pleasant and attractive in personality or manner

examples.en: Our charming tour guide made even the rainy campus walk enjoyable.
examples.zh: 我们那位「有魅力的」讲解员让雨中的校园漫步也变得有趣。

examples.en: My charming grandfather wins over every nurse at the clinic.
examples.zh: 我那「讨人喜欢的」爷爷总能赢得诊所护士的喜爱。

words.enDefinition: physically attractive in appearance

examples.en: My cousin is so good-looking that strangers ask to photograph him.
examples.zh: 我表哥长得太「好看」，连陌生人都会想给他拍照。

examples.en: He is good-looking, but his kindness makes him truly popular.
examples.zh: 他虽然「长得好看」，但真正让他受欢迎的是为人善良。

words.enDefinition: slightly fat in a pleasant, soft-looking way

examples.en: My chubby baby cousin laughs whenever anyone makes airplane noises.
examples.zh: 我那「胖乎乎的」小表弟一听到飞机的声音就咯咯笑。

examples.en: The chubby cat in our dorm building has three different feeding schedules.
examples.zh: 宿舍楼里那只「胖乎乎的」猫被三拨人按不同时间喂。

words.enDefinition: admire and respect someone older or more experienced

examples.en: I look up to my track coach because he never excuses laziness.
examples.zh: 我很「敬佩」我的田径教练，因为他从不纵容偷懒。

examples.en: Younger students look up to seniors who survived the same brutal course.
examples.zh: 学弟学妹们都很「敬佩」挺过同一门硬课的学长学姐。

words.enDefinition: think someone is less important or worthy

examples.en: Some seniors look down on easy electives, but they boosted my GPA.
examples.zh: 有些学长「看不起」好过的选修课，但这些课拉高了我的绩点。

examples.en: My grandmother taught us never to look down on any honest job.
examples.zh: 奶奶教我们永远不要「轻视」任何正当的职业。

words.enDefinition: become familiar with someone over time

examples.en: It took a month to really get to know my host sister.
examples.zh: 我花了一个月才和寄宿家庭的姐姐真正「熟悉起来」。

examples.en: Game nights are the fastest way to get to know your hallmates.
examples.zh: 游戏之夜是「认识」同楼层同学最快的方式。

collocations: a chance to get to know someone

words.enDefinition: form friendships with new people

examples.en: Joining the photography club helped me make friends outside my major.
examples.zh: 加入摄影社，让我交到了专业以外的「朋友」。

examples.en: It's easier to make friends when you ask people about themselves.
examples.zh: 多聊聊对方自己的事，就更容易「交到朋友」。

words.enDefinition: slowly become less close over time

examples.en: My best friend and I grew apart after we chose different universities.
examples.zh: 去了不同的大学之后，我和最好的朋友渐渐「疏远」了。

examples.en: Couples or friends grow apart when they stop sharing daily details.
examples.zh: 当彼此不再分享日常琐事，朋友就会渐渐「疏远」。

collocations: naturally grow apart over the years

words.enDefinition: stop contacting someone over time

examples.en: I lost touch with my middle school deskmate after moving cities.
examples.zh: 搬去另一个城市之后，我和初中同桌「断了联系」。

examples.en: Don't lose touch with your professors once the semester ends.
examples.zh: 学期结束后，也别和教授们「断了联系」。

words.enDefinition: have a serious argument that ends a friendship

examples.en: They fell out with their housemate over unpaid electricity bills.
examples.zh: 因为没人付电费，他们和合住的室友「闹掰」了。

examples.en: I fell out with my best friend once, but we made up a year later.
examples.zh: 我和挚友「闹翻」过一次，但一年后我们和好了。

collocations: fall out with a close friend

words.enDefinition: shout angrily at someone because you are upset

examples.en: The coach yelled at us for jogging through the warm-up drills.
examples.zh: 教练因为我们热身敷衍而「冲我们大吼」。

examples.en: My mom used to yell at me for leaving lights on everywhere.
examples.zh: 我妈以前总因为我到处不关灯「吼我」。

collocations: get yelled at by the coach

words.enDefinition: discuss someone negatively when they are not present

examples.en: It hurts when classmates talk behind your back about your grades.
examples.zh: 同学「背后议论」你的成绩，让人很难受。

examples.en: I'd rather hear criticism directly than have friends talk behind my back.
examples.zh: 我宁愿听直接的批评，也不愿朋友「在背后议论我」。

words.enDefinition: tell other people unverified stories about someone

examples.en: Someone spread rumors about a dorm inspection, and half the floor panicked.
examples.zh: 有人「散布谣言」说宿舍要检查，半层楼的人都慌了。

examples.en: Spreading rumors about roommates can destroy trust on a whole floor.
examples.zh: 「传室友的谣言」可能毁掉一整层楼的信任。

words.enDefinition: an unverified story passed from person to person

examples.en: The rumor about a surprise quiz spread through the group chat in minutes.
examples.zh: 关于突击测验的「谣言」几分钟就在群里传开了。

examples.en: Don't believe every rumor you hear in the dorm hallway.
examples.zh: 别相信宿舍走廊里听到的每一条「传闻」。

words.enDefinition: angrily criticize someone, often a child

examples.en: Mom scolded me for skipping family dinner to watch the game.
examples.zh: 我为了看球赛没吃家宴，被妈妈「训斥」了一顿。

examples.en: The landlady scolded us for microwaving fish in the shared kitchen.
examples.zh: 房东太太因为我们在公共厨房热鱼而「责骂」了我们。

words.enDefinition: share private feelings with someone you trust

examples.en: I confide in my older cousin because she never judges me.
examples.zh: 我喜欢向表姐「倾诉」，因为她从不评判我。

examples.en: Students rarely confide in professors, though office hours make it easier.
examples.zh: 学生很少向教授「吐露心事」，不过答疑时间让这变得容易。

collocations: have no one to confide in

words.enDefinition: rely on someone for emotional support in hard times

examples.en: During finals week, I lean on my older sister for encouragement.
examples.zh: 期末周，我会在情感上「依靠」姐姐给我打气。

examples.en: It's okay to lean on friends when homesickness hits hard.
examples.zh: 想家难熬的时候，「依靠」朋友没什么不可以。

words.enDefinition: go to someone for help when in trouble

examples.en: Whenever the lease confuses me, I turn to my cousin who studies law.
examples.zh: 每当看不懂租约，我都会向学法律的表哥「求助」。

examples.en: First-year students can turn to the dorm supervisor for any emergency.
examples.zh: 大一新生遇到紧急情况，可以「求助」宿舍管理员。

collocations: turn to your family for help
have no one to turn to

words.enDefinition: stay with someone so they feel less alone

examples.en: My roommate kept me company in the hospital waiting room all afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的室友在候诊室一直「陪伴」着我。

examples.en: I video call Grandma on weekends just to keep her company.
examples.zh: 我周末给奶奶打视频电话，只是为了「陪陪她」。

collocations: keep you company on the commute

words.enDefinition: quickly become friendly when you first meet

examples.en: My roommate and I hit it off over late-night instant noodles.
examples.zh: 我和室友深夜一起吃泡面，聊得「一见如故」。

examples.en: The two visiting students hit it off at the airport shuttle.
examples.zh: 两位来访学生在机场班车上「一拍即合」。

collocations: hit it off at a party
we hit it off right away

words.enDefinition: slowly begin to like someone you first felt unsure about

examples.en: The shy exchange student warmed up to our group after two game nights.
examples.zh: 玩了两晚桌游之后，那位交换生渐渐「喜欢上了」我们这群人。

examples.en: It took weeks for my cat to warm up to my new roommate.
examples.zh: 花了好几个星期，我的猫才渐渐「接受」我的新室友。

words.enDefinition: give someone the details they missed

examples.en: Fill me in on the group meeting; I was at the dentist.
examples.zh: 我去看牙了，你「跟我说说」组会的情况吧。

examples.en: My sister filled our parents in about the wedding date over dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭时，姐姐把婚期的安排「告知」了父母。

collocations: fill someone in on the plan

words.enDefinition: light polite conversation about unimportant topics

examples.en: Elevator small talk with neighbors usually covers weather and weekend plans.
examples.zh: 电梯里和邻居的「寒暄」通常离不开天气和周末安排。

examples.en: Making small talk at orientation helped me remember fifty new names.
examples.zh: 迎新会上的「闲聊」让我和五十个新同学混了个脸熟。

words.enDefinition: contact someone by phone, message or email

examples.en: Get in touch with your host family before your flight lands.
examples.zh: 航班落地之前，先和寄宿家庭「取得联系」。

examples.en: I got in touch with my old roommate through the alumni group.
examples.zh: 我通过校友群和以前的室友重新「联系上了」。

collocations: get in touch with the landlord

words.enDefinition: choose to support one person in a dispute

examples.en: When my two roommates argue, I refuse to take sides.
examples.zh: 两个室友吵架时，我拒绝「站队」。

examples.en: Parents shouldn't take sides when their kids quarrel over toys.
examples.zh: 孩子们为玩具争吵时，父母不该「偏袒任何一方」。

words.enDefinition: stay available to support someone in hard times

examples.en: My best friend was there for me through every homesick night.
examples.zh: 每个想家的夜晚，我的挚友都「在我身边」支持我。

examples.en: Promise you'll be there for each other during exam season.
examples.zh: 答应我，考试季你们要「互相支持」。

words.enDefinition: care for children until they are adults

examples.en: My grandparents raised me while my parents worked in another city.
examples.zh: 父母在外地工作时，是爷爷奶奶把我「抚养」大的。

examples.en: Raising three kids on a small shop's income took real discipline.
examples.zh: 靠小店的收入「抚养」三个孩子，需要极强的自律。

words.enDefinition: give someone the same name as another person

examples.en: I was named after my great-grandfather, who was a village doctor.
examples.zh: 我的名字「取自」曾祖父，他是村里的医生。

examples.en: Many campus buildings are named after the family who donated them.
examples.zh: 校园里许多大楼都以捐赠家族「命名」。

words.enDefinition: have a similar appearance to someone else

examples.en: People say I look like my dad, especially when I frown.
examples.zh: 大家说我「长得像」我爸，尤其是皱眉的时候。

examples.en: Do the twin sisters in your dorm look exactly like each other?
examples.zh: 你们宿舍那对双胞胎姐妹「长得一模一样」吗？

words.enDefinition: formally promise to marry someone, usually with a ring

examples.en: My brother got engaged on the ferris wheel last Saturday.
examples.zh: 上周六，我哥哥在摩天轮上和女友「订了婚」。

examples.en: They got engaged after dating for just six months at university.
examples.zh: 他们在大学里才交往六个月就「订婚」了。

collocations: get engaged to my college sweetheart

words.enDefinition: change from a child into an adult

examples.en: I grew up in a small town where everyone knew my family.
examples.zh: 我在一个大家都认识我家人的小镇「长大成人」。

examples.en: Kids who grow up with pets usually get along with others more easily.
examples.zh: 和宠物一起「长大」的孩子，通常更容易与人相处。

collocations: grow up in a small town
